title: orch config
description: Settings of the orch module: execution engine choice, default run-policy, work source, run-policy folders, events and the conductor.

engine.description: Execution engine used when neither a flag nor engine_by_role names one.

engine_by_role.description: Execution engine by role id; a role that is not listed uses the engine key.

default_profile.description: Run-policy used when the scenario of a task names none.

debug.description: Debug mode of conductor runs: a run reports DEBUG_MODE at its start with the observer protocol (packages/orch/dev-skills/orch-debug) and keeps a journal, a metrics table and findings in <run>/debug/. The roles and their prompts do not change. Set it per machine, per project, or with --debug/--no-debug for one run.

work_source.description: Id of the plugin of the extension point orch:work-source that supplies the work.

stale.description: What preparation does with a capability record that is past its freshness date: warn and go on, or refuse.

profiles.description: Run-policy packs beyond the ones shipped with orch.

dirs.description: Extra folders with run-policy packs (one folder per policy id): absolute paths or paths starting with ~. Machine-wide: a project file cannot set it, because it makes orch read files from the listed paths.

enabled.description: Whether orch emits the orch.run.* events.

conductor.description: The conductor (orch conduct): the global layer of the run options and how roles start.

provider.description: Provider of every role whose stage names none.

registrar.description: Actor PROVIDER/MODEL that registers outcomes in the work source.

rules.description: Rules for the executor of every run; the options of the pack, the phase and the item append theirs.

session_executor.description: How the executor sessions are shared inside one run of several pieces (the first run-options layer, `session.executor`): `handoff` gives each piece a fresh session with the handoff of the earlier pieces, `shared` resumes the session of the previous executor, `per-item` starts a fresh one for every step.

on_blocked.description: What a blocked piece of work does to the run: stop it, or report it and go on.

questions.description: What a blocking question of the executor does: queue (the piece is blocked QUESTION and waits for orch conduct answer), deny (blocked QUESTION_DENIED, no answer expected), defaults (a question with a default is answered by it once, by policy; without one it is queued) or advisor (the advisor role gives advice; advice that needs no owner answers the question by advisor, any other is queued with the advice; needs orch.advisor.enabled).

tokens_max.description: Fresh tokens of a piece of work past which a BUDGET_OVER beacon is printed (nothing is stopped); 0 means none.

stage_timeout_s.description: Ceiling on the whole run of one role in seconds; 0 has none for a streaming role (STAGE_SLOW beacons report a long run) and keeps the launch catalog timeout for a text role.

stage_idle_timeout_s.description: A streaming role is stopped when its output has not grown for this many seconds (a hang, not a long run); 0 never stops it; default 5400. STAGE_IDLE beacons report shorter silences and what runs meanwhile.

check_timeout_s.description: Ceiling on one acceptance check in seconds; 0 (default) has none: CHECK_SLOW beacons report a long check.

check_idle_timeout_s.description: An acceptance check is stopped when its log has not grown for this many seconds (a hung test runner); 0 never stops it; default 3600.

argv.description: Command line of a role instead of the launch catalog entry, by role id ({model}, {effort}, {cwd} and {orch} are filled in). Machine-wide: a project file cannot set it, because it chooses the commands the conductor runs.

risk.description: The risk score of a piece after its executor round (P7.2): a piece whose run policy has no review gets one when the score reaches `review.dynamic_threshold` of the run options. Weights add up (capped at 100); a weight of 0 turns a feature off.

public_cli.description: A path of `patterns.public_cli` changed (a public command line).

shared.description: A path of `patterns.shared` changed (a module others import).

red_first.description: An acceptance check was red in the first executor round.

outside_write_set.description: Paths outside the write set changed.

patterns.description: Repository path patterns of the features (`*` inside a segment, `**` any segments, a trailing `/` owns everything below).

diff_lines.description: Changed lines past which the diff_size feature counts.

critical.description: Features that add the review on their own, whatever the score (REVIEW_ADDED names them); [] leaves only the threshold.

skills_bridge.description: Command of the skills bridge, run as a process with `--select ...` when the run options give a role `skills: ["auto"]`; empty means no bridge, and `auto` then stops the piece with SKILLS_BRIDGE_UNAVAILABLE. Machine-wide: a project file cannot set it, because it chooses the command the conductor runs.

research.description: Research sources (P10.1): where the researcher role and `orch.py research query` look things up.

policy.description: When a piece of work gets a research stage: required (every piece), conditional (a piece whose research need is required) or off (never).

sources.description: Research sources by id. An argv chooses the process orch starts, so only the machine, the invocation file and flags may set it; a project file may name roots and limits.

kind.description: Adapter: command (argv, the query on stdin, JSON on stdout), filesystem (a search over roots) or mcp-stdio (an MCP server over stdio, the query goes to its tool).

argv.description: Command and arguments of a command or mcp-stdio source (required by both kinds on the merged layers: SOURCE_INVALID otherwise); a leading ~ is expanded. Machine-wide: a project file cannot set it, because it chooses the commands orch runs.

tool.description: mcp-stdio: name of the tool that receives the query.

roots.description: filesystem: folders searched, absolute, starting with ~, or relative to the project (required by this kind on the merged layers: SOURCE_INVALID otherwise).

timeout_s.description: Ceiling on one query in seconds.

concurrency.description: Queries of this source that run at once in one orch process.

order.description: Place on the ladder of sources: lower first, ties by id.

advisor.description: The advisor role (P10.4): one opinion on a blocking question (questions = advisor), on acceptance checks that stay red after the check_fixes corrections, and on a Major finding the triager rejected.

enabled.description: Whether the conductor asks the advisor at all. Off: every trigger behaves as before.

max_rounds.description: Advice rounds per piece of work, all triggers together; past it the problem is handled as without the advisor.

human_gate.description: Advice categories that are never applied without the owner: the problem is queued with the advice instead.

stubs.description: Stubs: additional instructions for the roles (`orch stubs publish|list|show`), from `~/.config/swissknifeman/stubs` (machine) and `<project>/.swissknifeman/stubs` (project). A run resolves them once and keeps the snapshot. Machine-wide: a project cannot turn its own stubs on or widen what it may add.

enabled.description: Whether the role prompts get the stubs at all.

layers.description: Layers read: a machine that runs repositories it does not trust leaves `project` out, so their stubs never reach a model.
